SeasonResult: St. Andrew's defeated James Island Christian 4-1 at Porter-Gaud to win the SCISA Class AA boys soccer championship and finish 15-1.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. NewsBank confirms the 15-1 final record, 80-8 scoring margin entering the state final, and 84-9 final scoring margin. The schedule now includes five record-path placeholders: three unreported wins between Apr. 5-29, a broad-search Patrick Henry result from early May with exact citation pending, and one additional early-May unreported win before the May 9 Harvest Baptist result.
HistoricalSummary: St. Andrew's restored the boys soccer championship standard in Spring 2003, going 15-1 and winning the SCISA Class AA title under Mark Gibbons. The recovered NewsBank results begin with a 15-0 win over Jefferson Davis Academy and continue through region wins over Harvest Baptist, James Island Christian, Patrick Henry, Hilton Head Prep, and Cathedral Academy.

The Saints' only loss came at James Island Christian on April 4, a 3-2 double-overtime result that split the regular-season series. Published record lines show three additional wins between that 3-1 record and the Apr. 30 Patrick Henry win that moved St. Andrew's to 7-1, so the schedule now carries three late-April placeholders in that gap.

An early-May broad-search result also surfaced a 6-0 win at Patrick Henry in Estill, with Beau Hinton scoring three goals and Jacob Rauers scoring twice. One more early-May placeholder is needed before the May 9 Harvest Baptist win, which listed St. Andrew's at 11-1.

The state tournament run was decisive. St. Andrew's beat The King's Academy 10-1 in the quarterfinals, edged Harvest Baptist 2-1 in the semifinal, and defeated James Island Christian 4-1 in the championship match at Porter-Gaud. Jacob Rauers scored a hat trick in the final after moving from midfield to forward, while Lyle McKenzie added the opening goal.

The championship was St. Andrew's fourth SCISA boys soccer title in six seasons, joining the 1998, 1999, and 2000 teams. The preview before the final listed Lyle McKenzie with 17 goals and 9 assists, Beau Hinton with 15 goals and 3 assists, Omar Glenn with 12 goals and 6 assists, and Jacob Rauers with 7 goals and 10 assists before Rauers' title-game hat trick.
HighlightNotes: SCISA Class AA state champion with a 15-1 final record.
SCISA Region 1 champion and top seed for the state tournament.
St. Andrew's outscored opponents 84-9, including 80-8 before the state final.
Jacob Rauers scored three goals in the championship win over James Island Christian.
Lyle McKenzie, Beau Hinton, Omar Glenn, and Jacob Rauers were the leading scorers in the recovered season record.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's won its second straight SCISA Class A/AA boys soccer championship with a 5-1 win over James Island Christian at Heathwood Hall.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. The season currently includes 12 known games, including an inferred May 8 region championship win over Beaufort Academy with no reported score. HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2004 boys soccer archive currently begins with St. Andrew's 4-1 region win over Cathedral Academy on March 22, 2004, followed by wins over Charleston Collegiate, Beaufort Academy, and James Island Christian, a 3-3 tie against Hilton Head Christian, an 8-0 win over Patrick Henry, region tournament wins over Cathedral Academy and Patrick Henry Academy, an inferred region championship win over Beaufort Academy, and state tournament wins over St. Francis Xavier, Cathedral Academy, and James Island Christian.

Hamish Huntley scored twice in the March 22 Cathedral Academy win, the March 23 Charleston Collegiate win, the April 6 Hilton Head Christian tie, the April 29 Patrick Henry win, and the May 4 Cathedral Academy win, then scored five goals against Patrick Henry Academy on May 6.

The May 8 region championship result was not reported, but the May 10 state tournament brief listed St. Andrew's at 10-1-1 after a 9-0 quarterfinal win over St. Francis Xavier. That record line indicates St. Andrew's won the May 8 region title match.
The May 12 Savannah Morning News recap listed St. Andrew's at 12-1-1 after a 7-1 state semifinal win over Cathedral Academy, sending the Saints to the SCISA Class AA/A championship match.
St. Andrew's defeated James Island Christian 5-1 on May 15 at Heathwood Hall to win its second straight SCISA Class A/AA boys soccer championship and finish 13-1-1.

SeasonResult: St. Andrew's went 3-6 in Spring 2005, earned the top spot from SCISA Region 1-AA, and exited the SCISA Class AA state tournament against Byrnes Academy.
StatusNote: Archive build in progress. The recovered NewsBank lines identify eight scored games plus one placeholder win needed to reconcile the May 12 Savannah Morning News final record of 3-6. HistoricalSummary: The Spring 2005 boys soccer archive now begins with St. Andrew's 3-2 penalty-kick win over Cathedral Academy on April 4. Hamish Huntley scored twice, Kevin Crouch, Ryan Kirby, and Chris Rauers had assists, and Emmett Eason made six saves.

St. Andrew's then dropped non-region games to Pinewood Prep, Beaufort Academy, Beaufort Academy again, Pinewood Prep, and Hilton Head Prep. Huntley scored at Hilton Head Prep, and Ben Harrison scored against Pinewood Prep on a Huntley assist.

The Saints closed region play with a 2-1 win over Cathedral Academy on May 6. Chris Rauers and Brian Crouch scored, Kevin Crouch assisted, and Emmett Eason made six saves as St. Andrew's moved to 2-0 in SCISA Region 1-AA and earned the region's top state-tournament seed.

The May 12 Savannah Morning News listed St. Andrew's at 3-6 after a 2-0 SCISA Class AA state tournament loss to Byrnes Academy. One win remains unidentified in the recovered schedule, so the game list includes a placeholder until that score is found.
